## 3.3 Next-token prediction and sampling

**Aim.** The reader understands that the model outputs a probability distribution over the next token, that text is generated by sampling one token at a time and feeding it back in, and what temperature and top-p sampling do.

**Text (draft).**

> At each position, the transformer's last layer produces a score, called a logit, for every token in the vocabulary. Softmax turns the scores into probabilities. During training this distribution is scored against the token that actually came next (Section 2.5).
>
> To generate text, the model computes the distribution for the next token, one token is sampled from it, the token is appended to the input, and the process repeats. Everything a chat model writes is produced this way, one token at a time.
>
> Two settings change the sampling. Temperature T divides the logits before softmax. T below 1 concentrates probability on the most likely tokens, and T above 1 spreads it out. Top-p sampling keeps only the most probable tokens whose probabilities add up to p, and samples among those.

**Formula.**

```latex
p_i = \frac{\exp(z_i / T)}{\sum_j \exp(z_j / T)}
```

**Image.** Bar charts of the ten most likely next tokens after "The capital of France is", at T = 0.5, 1, and 2.

**Interactive: "Sample the next token".**

- Display: a bar chart of the 20 most likely next tokens; the generated text so far, with each token's probability at the time it was chosen.
- Controls: prompt menu; temperature; top-p; Sample (one token); Greedy (take the most likely); Reset.
- Try: (1) Generate at T = 0 several times and compare. (2) Generate at T = 1.5 and watch the text drift. (3) Find a prompt where the model is nearly certain and one where it is unsure.
- What to notice: any one answer from a model is a single draw from a distribution.
- Build: live with a small model run in the browser (distilgpt2 through transformers.js), with a precomputed fallback; medium.

**Check.** At a temperature near 0, what does sampling become? Answer: always choosing the most likely token (greedy decoding).

**Links.** Back to 2.5; forward to 4.3 (changing the distribution with a reward). References: Holtzman et al. (2020), on top-p sampling.

**Changes made while building (2026-10-16).**

- Built 2026-11-06 under the brief's addendum. The spec's build (distilgpt2 live through transformers.js) conflicts with the addendum's rule that the browser computes nothing that needs the model, so GPT-2 small's distributions were computed in advance (`tools/3-3/`, revision 607a30d, 1.8 MB). For each prompt: a tree of about 2,400 prefixes, each with GPT-2's 20 most likely next tokens and enough summary numbers to give their exact probabilities at any temperature on the grid 0, 0.25, ..., 2; and four whole 30-token continuations that GPT-2 sampled at each temperature with top-p 0.5, 0.9, and 1, plus the greedy continuation.
- Because the tree cannot hold every possible continuation, Sample draws only among tokens whose next step is stored, in proportion to GPT-2's probabilities; the readout gives the probability those tokens hold, and the panel note says what is precomputed. At T = 1 the stored tree lets the tool generate a median of 3 to 9 tokens depending on the prompt; at T = 0, 24 tokens. Task 2 (drift at T = 1.5) uses the whole continuations sampled by GPT-2 itself, since the tree is built for T near 1.
- Temperature is a slider in steps of 0.25 and top-p in steps of 0.1, so the stored numbers stay small. Top-p is applied after temperature, as in Hugging Face's sampler.
- Prompts: "The capital of France is", "Once upon a time", "1, 2, 3, 4,", "Thank you very", "My favorite food is". GPT-2 small gives " Paris" only 0.032 after "The capital of France is" (" the" 0.085); task 3 uses this, with "Thank you very" (" much" 0.992) as the nearly certain prompt.
- Added task 4 on top-p (three tokens kept at T = 1, top-p 0.5, after "Once upon a time"). Task 1 found that greedy decoding loops ("the chicken. I love the chicken. ..."), which the text after the tasks ties to Holtzman et al. (2020).
- Whole continuations containing profanity or sexual-violence words are drawn again with a new seed (3 of 120 sets were); the distributions are not filtered. Some stored GPT-2 outputs contain an em dash, which is model text and was left as generated.
- Two checks added: a temperature computation by hand (logits 2 and 1 at T = 0.5 gives 0.88), and what two different answers to the same question show.
